title: ENDEX: Hospital at Level 1 — Record in Doubt

fields.resolution: ENDEX. It is now 20:45 on Friday, March 13, 2026. The core switch replacement has not yet been installed. The EHR remains read-only; registration, PACS, and secure messaging are still down. The paper record is the only active record. Six patients have been transferred out. Three expectant patients are receiving comfort care. The reconciliation of dual patient identities and the lab result backlog remain unresolved. This concludes the exercise.
finalState: The hospital remains at Level 1 for the night.
The EHR is read-only; registration and PACS remain down.
The paper record is the only active record.
Six patients have been transferred out.
Three expectant patients are receiving comfort care.
Patient identity reconciliation and lab result backlog have not begun.
fields.hotWashTransition: Thank you, everyone. Put down your phones and radios. We will take ten minutes, then start the hot wash.
fields.hotWashMethod: 3-Up, 3-Down: three things that went well, three things that broke
hotWashQuestions: How did the team manage patient identification during dual numbering and what could have prevented it?
What were the risks of using paper records in a surge with incomplete system recovery?
How effective was the communication of the crisis standards of care to staff and families?
What challenges arose in coordinating with external agencies during the EHR downtime?
How might the hospital have improved the lab result reconciliation process under pressure?
